passage: The octopus is one of the most intelligent animals in the ocean. Although it has no bones and lives alone, it can solve problems that puzzle many other creatures. In laboratory experiments, octopuses have learned to unscrew jar lids to reach food hidden inside. Some have even escaped from their tanks at night by squeezing through tiny gaps, only to be found the next morning in a nearby room. Scientists are particularly interested in how the octopus thinks, because its brain is built very differently from ours. Roughly two thirds of its neurons are located in its eight arms, which means each arm can make some decisions on its own. This unusual design allows the animal to taste, touch, and explore objects at the same time. Researchers hope that studying octopuses will help engineers create flexible robots that can move through narrow spaces. Despite their talents, octopuses live only a few years, so they cannot pass their knowledge on to their young.

passage: Parks and gardens are often seen as pleasant extras in a city, but research suggests they are much more than that. Trees reduce summer temperatures by providing shade and releasing moisture into the air. Grass and soil absorb rainwater, which lowers the risk of flooding during heavy storms. Green spaces also benefit people directly: studies show that residents who live near a park walk more, report lower stress, and feel more connected to their neighbors. Despite these advantages, land in city centers is expensive, and developers frequently prefer to build offices or apartments. Some planners have responded with creative solutions, such as planting gardens on rooftops and covering the walls of buildings with climbing plants. These projects use small amounts of space yet still deliver cooling, cleaner air, and a place for birds and insects to live. Critics argue that rooftop gardens are costly to maintain, but supporters point out that they also reduce energy bills by insulating buildings.

Its rulers wanted to collect all the knowledge of humanity, so they ordered that every ship entering the harbor be searched for books. Any scroll found on board was copied, and the owner often received the copy while the library kept the original. Scholars from many countries came to work there, and they made important advances in geography, mathematics, and medicine. One of them calculated the size of the Earth with surprising accuracy by measuring shadows in two different cities. Historians still debate how the library finally disappeared. Some say a single fire destroyed it, while others believe it declined slowly over centuries as funding was reduced and scholars left. What is certain is that the loss of so many writings made it harder for later generations to understand the ancient world.

Hormones that make us sleepy are released later at night in teenagers than in children or adults, so a teenager may not feel tired until eleven o'clock or after. When school starts at seven or eight in the morning, students lose valuable hours of sleep and may find it hard to concentrate. Several schools have experimented with starting the day an hour later. In these schools, attendance improved, students reported feeling happier, and test scores rose slightly. Not everyone supports the change, however. One answer is desalination, a process that removes salt from seawater so that it can be drunk or used for farming. The most common method forces seawater through extremely thin filters that block salt but let water pass. Desalination plants now supply drinking water to millions of people in dry regions such as the Arabian Peninsula. The technology is not perfect, however. It uses large amounts of electricity, and the salty water left over, called brine, can harm sea life if it is released carelessly. To reduce these problems, engineers are building plants powered by solar energy and developing ways to spread the brine over wide areas so it mixes safely with the ocean. If these improvements succeed, desalination could become a reliable and sustainable source of water for many communities in the future.

A reef is built by tiny animals called polyps, which form hard skeletons around themselves and slowly create large structures over thousands of years. Polyps live in partnership with algae, microscopic plants that give corals their bright colors and provide food through photosynthesis. This partnership is delicate. If the water becomes too warm, the polyps push the algae out, and the coral turns white in a process known as bleaching. A bleached reef is not necessarily dead, but it is weak and can starve if conditions do not improve quickly. Reefs also protect coasts by absorbing the force of waves, and they provide food and income for millions of people. Conservation groups therefore encourage visitors to avoid touching coral, to use sunscreens that do not harm marine life, and to support projects that grow new coral in nurseries.

Another challenge is space: a farm that powers a small city may cover several square kilometers. Some designers solve this by floating panels on reservoirs, where they also reduce evaporation, or by installing them above parking lots. Households can also benefit. passage: Most students prepare for exams by reading their notes many times the night before. This method, often called cramming, feels productive, but psychologists have found that it produces weak long-term memory. A far better strategy is spaced repetition, which means reviewing the same material several times with gaps between sessions. The first review might happen the next day, the second after a week, and the third after a month. Each time you struggle slightly to remember, the connection in your brain becomes stronger. Another powerful technique is self-testing. Instead of rereading a chapter, close the book and try to write down everything you remember. The effort may feel uncomfortable, but studies show that students who test themselves score higher than those who only reread. Of course, no method can replace understanding. Memorizing facts without knowing how they connect will not help much if the exam asks you to apply ideas to a new situation.

During that time he traveled through North Africa, the Middle East, Central Asia, India, China, and parts of East and West Africa, covering roughly 120,000 kilometers. He generally traveled with caravans or on merchant ships, and he relied on the hospitality of local communities, scholars, and rulers. Because he was trained as a judge, he was often offered work along the way, which helped to pay for the journey. After returning, he dictated an account of his adventures to a writer, and the resulting book remains one of the most valuable sources about the fourteenth-century world. Modern historians sometimes question certain details, noting that he may have borrowed descriptions from earlier writers. Nevertheless, his travel record is impressive, and it shows how connected distant regions already were centuries ago.

Rather than making buildings completely rigid, modern designs allow them to move slightly. Rubber and steel pads placed under the foundation absorb shaking, while heavy weights near the top, known as dampers, swing in the opposite direction to reduce sway. Many old temples use a similar idea: the famous five-story pagodas have a flexible central pillar that has helped them stand for centuries. Building codes in Japan are also strict, and they are updated after every major disaster. In addition, schools regularly practice drills so that children know how to protect themselves. Visitors are often surprised that life in tall buildings feels calm even when the ground trembles. Although no building can be completely safe, careful design, regular inspection, and public education greatly reduce the damage and save thousands of lives.

passage: Describe a skill you learned outside school. Write for 5 minutes.
model: One skill I learned outside school is cooking. When I was fifteen, my mother started teaching me simple dishes on weekends, and I quickly became interested. At first I made many mistakes, such as burning rice or adding too much salt, but she encouraged me to keep trying. I also watched short videos and wrote down recipes in a small notebook. Over time, I learned how to plan a meal, manage my time, and clean up afterwards. Today I can prepare dinner for my family without help. This skill has made me more independent and patient, and it has also given me a relaxing hobby. I believe everyone should learn to cook, because it is useful for life and brings people together around the table.
tips: Empieza con una frase que responda directamente a la consigna.
Escribe sin parar los 5 minutos y deja 30 segundos para revisar ortografía.
Varía las estructuras: mezcla frases cortas y largas con conectores (however, because, although).

passage: Describe a place in your city that you like to visit. Write for 5 minutes.
model: My favorite place in my city is the old botanical garden near the river. I usually go there on Saturday mornings, when the air is fresh and the paths are quiet. The garden has hundreds of plants from different countries, a small pond with ducks, and a wooden bridge where I like to sit and read. What I enjoy most is the sense of calm; after a busy week of study, walking among the trees helps me relax and organize my thoughts. Sometimes I bring a notebook and write down ideas for my projects. The entrance is cheap, so students can visit often. I would recommend it to any visitor who wants to escape the noise of the city for a few hours.
tips: Describe con detalles sensoriales (qué ves, qué oyes) para sonar natural.
Varía las estructuras: mezcla frases cortas y largas con conectores (however, because, although).
Apunta a 100 palabras o más; más texto bien escrito suma puntos.

passage: Write about a person who taught you something important. Write for 5 minutes.
model: The person who taught me the most important lesson is my grandfather. He worked as a carpenter for forty years, and he always said that quality needs patience. When I was twelve, he asked me to help him build a small table. I wanted to finish quickly, so I cut the wood carelessly, and the legs did not fit. Instead of getting angry, he calmly showed me how to measure twice before cutting once. We started again, and the second table was beautiful. That day I understood that rushing usually costs more time than working carefully. I still remember his advice when I study for exams or begin a new project. Thanks to him, I try to do every task with attention and respect for the details.
tips: Cuenta una pequeña anécdota: una historia corta hace tu texto más convincente.
Apunta a 100 palabras o más; más texto bien escrito suma puntos.
Escribe sin parar los 5 minutos y deja 30 segundos para revisar ortografía.

passage: Describe a trip you would like to take and explain why. Write for 5 minutes.
model: I would love to travel to Turkey and visit Istanbul and Cappadocia. I am fascinated by the history of Istanbul, a city where Europe and Asia meet and where ancient mosques, markets, and palaces stand beside modern streets. I would also like to see the unusual rock formations of Cappadocia and watch the sunrise from a balloon ride. Another reason is the food: I have heard that the fresh bread, grilled vegetables, and sweet desserts are delicious. I would travel in spring, when the weather is mild, and I would stay in small family hotels to meet local people. Before going, I plan to learn a few Turkish phrases. For me, a good trip is not only about sightseeing but also about learning from other cultures.
tips: Usa conectores (Another reason is..., Before going...) para ordenar las ideas.
Escribe sin parar los 5 minutos y deja 30 segundos para revisar ortografía.
Varía las estructuras: mezcla frases cortas y largas con conectores (however, because, although).

passage: Describe your daily routine and one thing you would like to change. Write for 5 minutes.
model: My day usually begins at six, when I wake up for the morning prayer and prepare a simple breakfast. After that, I commute to the university, where I attend classes until three. In the afternoon, I study in the library or do some exercise, and in the evening I have dinner with my family and review my notes. I generally go to bed around eleven. If I could change one thing, I would spend less time on my phone. Many evenings I check messages and videos for an hour without noticing, and that time could be used for reading or sleeping earlier. Recently I started leaving the phone in another room after nine o'clock, and I already feel more rested and focused.
tips: Usa presente simple y adverbios de frecuencia (usually, generally) para rutinas.
Varía las estructuras: mezcla frases cortas y largas con conectores (however, because, although).
Apunta a 100 palabras o más; más texto bien escrito suma puntos.

passage: Describe a useful piece of technology that you use every day. Write for 5 minutes.
model: The technology I use most every day is my smartphone. I rely on it for many tasks: setting alarms, checking the weather, translating words, and keeping a calendar of my classes. It also lets me contact my family quickly when I am far away. One feature I find especially useful is the offline map, because it helps me find my way in new cities without an internet connection. However, I am aware of the risks. If I use it without control, it distracts me from my studies. For this reason, I turned off most notifications and set a daily time limit for entertainment apps. Used wisely, a smartphone is like a small library, office, and guide that fits in my pocket.
tips: Muestra equilibrio: ventaja + límite o riesgo. Eso demuestra nivel alto.
Apunta a 100 palabras o más; más texto bien escrito suma puntos.
Escribe sin parar los 5 minutos y deja 30 segundos para revisar ortografía.

passage: Write about a meal or tradition your family enjoys together. Write for 5 minutes.
model: Every Friday evening, my family gathers for a large dinner at my grandparents' house. My grandmother prepares rice with vegetables, grilled chicken, and a fresh salad, while the children help set the table. Before eating, we share what we are grateful for that week, and my grandfather tells a short story from his childhood. I love this tradition because it makes us talk to each other without phones or television. Cousins who live in different cities often travel to join us, and the house becomes warm and noisy. After dinner we drink tea and play simple board games. This weekly meeting reminds me that family is a source of support, and I hope to continue the tradition with my own children someday.
tips: Escribe en presente para tradiciones y añade una emoción (I love this because...).
Escribe sin parar los 5 minutos y deja 30 segundos para revisar ortografía.
Varía las estructuras: mezcla frases cortas y largas con conectores (however, because, although).

passage: Describe a goal you want to achieve this year. Write for 5 minutes.
model: My main goal this year is to improve my English enough to study abroad. At the moment I can understand most conversations, but I still hesitate when I speak and make mistakes in grammar. To reach my goal, I have made a clear plan. Every morning I read one article and write ten new words in a notebook. Three times a week I practice speaking with a language partner online, and on weekends I watch a documentary without subtitles. I also take a practice test once a month to measure my progress. Achieving this goal will not be easy, but I am determined. Learning English will open doors to universities, scholarships, and friendships around the world.
tips: Un objetivo + plan concreto con pasos y frecuencia suena más convincente.
Varía las estructuras: mezcla frases cortas y largas con conectores (however, because, although).
Apunta a 100 palabras o más; más texto bien escrito suma puntos.

passage: Some people think students should wear school uniforms. Do you agree or disagree? Explain your opinion. Write for 5 minutes.
model: I agree that students should wear school uniforms, mainly because they promote equality and reduce distractions. When everyone dresses the same way, nobody feels pressure to own expensive clothes, so students can focus on learning instead of fashion. Uniforms also save time in the morning and money for families, who do not need to buy a large wardrobe. Furthermore, wearing a uniform creates a sense of belonging, which can improve discipline and school spirit. Of course, some people argue that uniforms limit self-expression. That is a fair concern, but I believe students can express their personality through their ideas, projects, and hobbies rather than clothing. Schools could also allow casual days once a month so that students enjoy some variety. All things considered, the benefits of uniforms outweigh the disadvantages, and I would support them in any school. In my own experience, students in uniform seem more serious about class, and teachers spend less time correcting small problems. Simple rules like this can make school a calmer and fairer place for everyone.
tips: Define tu postura en la primera frase (I agree/I disagree) y repítela al final.
Estructura: opinión, dos razones con ejemplos, una objeción y conclusión.
Revisa concordancia verbal y artículos; los errores pequeños restan menos si el texto es largo y claro.

passage: Is it better to live in a big city or in a small town? Give reasons for your answer. Write for 5 minutes.
model: In my opinion, a small town is better for most people, although big cities have clear advantages. In a small town, life is calmer and more affordable. Housing costs less, traffic is light, and neighbors usually know each other, which creates a strong sense of community. Children can play outside safely, and the air is cleaner. On the other hand, big cities offer more jobs, universities, hospitals, and cultural events, and public transportation makes it easy to move around. Young people who want to build a career often find more opportunities there. Nevertheless, modern technology allows many professionals to work remotely, so living far from a city is becoming more realistic. For this reason, I would choose a small town with a good internet connection. It offers peace and space while still allowing me to access the opportunities of the wider world. My own experience agrees with this: when I visit relatives in the countryside, I sleep better and feel less stressed. Of course, every person is different, but peace of mind is worth more to me than a busy social life.
tips: Concede un punto al otro lado (On the other hand) y luego refuérzalo con tu opinión.
Estructura: opinión, dos razones con ejemplos, una objeción y conclusión.
Revisa concordancia verbal y artículos; los errores pequeños restan menos si el texto es largo y claro.

passage: Should children have a daily limit on screen time? Explain your opinion. Write for 5 minutes.
model: Yes, I believe children should have a daily limit on screen time. First, too much time in front of screens can harm their health. Children who sit for hours often sleep badly, exercise less, and have trouble paying attention at school. Second, real-life activities, such as playing outside, reading books, and talking with family, help them develop social skills and creativity. Some parents argue that screens are educational, and this is partly true, since there are excellent apps for learning languages and science. However, the key is balance. I think one or two hours of quality content a day is reasonable, and parents should watch together with their children whenever possible. It is also important to set a good example: if adults constantly check their phones, children will copy them. With clear rules and open conversations, families can enjoy technology without letting it control their lives. Finally, parents should talk with children about why limits exist, so that rules feel fair instead of strict. When children understand the reasons, they usually follow them more willingly and develop self-control for the future.
tips: Usa ordinales (First, Second) para estructurar y una frase de contraste (However).
Estructura: opinión, dos razones con ejemplos, una objeción y conclusión.
Revisa concordancia verbal y artículos; los errores pequeños restan menos si el texto es largo y claro.

passage: Is working from home better than working in an office? Explain your opinion. Write for 5 minutes.
model: I think working from home is better for most people, but a mixture of both is ideal. At home, employees save the time and money they would spend commuting, and they can organize their schedule more flexibly. Many people also feel more productive in a quiet environment, away from constant interruptions. In addition, companies can hire talented workers from any city or country. However, working from home has disadvantages. Some people feel lonely, and it can be hard to separate work from family life. Teamwork may also suffer if colleagues never meet in person. For these reasons, I would prefer two or three days at home and the rest in the office. This arrangement keeps the freedom of remote work while maintaining personal contact and collaboration. Companies that offer this flexibility will probably keep happier and more loyal employees. Personally, I work better when I can start my day without a long trip, and I still enjoy meeting my team face to face. A flexible schedule gives me the best of both worlds and makes me more motivated.
tips: Una opinión matizada (mixture of both) puede ser tan válida como una extrema si la justificas.
Estructura: opinión, dos razones con ejemplos, una objeción y conclusión.
Revisa concordancia verbal y artículos; los errores pequeños restan menos si el texto es largo y claro.

passage: Should public transportation be free for everyone? Give your opinion with reasons. Write for 5 minutes.
model: I partly agree that public transportation should be free, at least for certain groups. Free buses and trains would help low-income families, students, and elderly people, who often struggle with the cost of tickets. It would also encourage more people to leave their cars at home, which would reduce traffic, noise, and air pollution. Cities such as Tallinn have already tested this idea with positive results. Nevertheless, there are serious drawbacks. Public transport is expensive to build and maintain, and without ticket income, the government would need to raise taxes or reduce other services. Moreover, if the system becomes overcrowded, quality could decline. Therefore, I believe the best solution is a low fixed fee, with free travel for children, students, and seniors. This policy keeps the system financially stable while making transportation accessible to the people who need it most. In the end, a good transport system is a public service, like roads or schools, and society benefits when more people can use it. A fair price is a small investment for cleaner and more connected cities.
tips: Propón una solución intermedia al final; demuestra pensamiento crítico.
Estructura: opinión, dos razones con ejemplos, una objeción y conclusión.
Revisa concordancia verbal y artículos; los errores pequeños restan menos si el texto es largo y claro.

passage: Is it more important to study what you love or what will earn the most money? Give your opinion. Write for 5 minutes.
model: In my view, it is more important to study what you love, as long as you have a realistic plan. When you enjoy a subject, you study harder, learn faster, and keep going when things become difficult. That passion often leads to excellence, and excellent professionals are usually rewarded with good opportunities. By contrast, people who choose a career only for money may feel bored or exhausted after a few years, which affects their health and happiness. That said, we cannot ignore practical needs. Everyone must be able to support a family and contribute to society. Therefore, students should research the job market and combine their interests with useful skills. For example, someone who loves art can learn digital design, and a person who enjoys languages can become a translator or teacher. In this way, it is possible to follow your passion and still build a stable future. Many successful people say that they were willing to work hard because they believed in their field. If students choose carefully and stay disciplined, passion and income do not have to be opposites.
tips: Incluye un ejemplo concreto (For example, ...) para reforzar tu argumento.
Estructura: opinión, dos razones con ejemplos, una objeción y conclusión.
Revisa concordancia verbal y artículos; los errores pequeños restan menos si el texto es largo y claro.

passage: Talk about a time when you helped someone. Speak for at least 30 seconds.
audio: Talk about a time when you helped someone. Speak for at least 30 seconds.
model: I would like to talk about a time when I helped a classmate who was struggling with math. Last year, my friend Omar failed the first exam of the semester, and he felt discouraged. I noticed that he understood the ideas when I explained them in simple words, so I offered to study with him. We met in the library twice a week for about an hour. I prepared easy examples, and we solved problems step by step. At first he made many mistakes, but he never gave up, and little by little he gained confidence. By the end of the semester, he passed the final exam with a very good grade. I felt extremely happy, because helping him also made me understand the subject better. That experience taught me that sharing knowledge benefits both people, and I now try to help others whenever I can.
tips: Habla sin pausas largas: mejor una frase sencilla y fluida que una compleja con dudas.
